newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended firmer with sentiment supported by early trade short covering. However, traders said London's reaction to rallying New York arabica prices was surprisingly muted. November added $19 to close at $1,514, while January shed $2 to close at $1,441. In New York arabica futures closed higher led by a sharp advance in the spot contract, amid persistent concerns about near-term supplies. This week's rally in New York had been fuelled by a surprise 10,000 60-kg bag draw in US certified stocks to 31,000 bags last week. However, what is more important is the fact that there is no fresh coffee awaiting certification in New York. Further US certified data are due on Monday. While origin selling has kept a lid on the gains, traders said the squeeze on the spot month would persist until more coffee began to flow in from Latin America near the end of 1996. The sharp downturn in stocks comes just as roasters move into their heaviest processing period in October and November and held New York spot differentials firm. December added 2.35 cents/lb to close at 109.80 cents/lb, while March closed 1.85 cents/lb higher at 104.15. The December/March differential widened to 5.65 cents/lb.

GUATEMALA - Guatemala exported 98,772 bags of coffee in September 1996, down 61 percent from the 251,879 bags exported in September 1995 and 37 percent below the 157,662 bags exported in August 1996. This brought coffee exports in the last quarter of 1995/96 (July/September) up to 446,107 bags compared to 882,449 bags exported the same quarter in 1995. Industry sources said exports have been down for several months because 90 percent of the 1995/96 harvest had been sold by June.

VIETNAM - Coffee production in 1996/97 (October/September) will be very much higher than had been forecast so far. Hoang Thanh Teim, vice director of the Coffee Research Institute, told Reuters that production in 1996/97 is estimated at 4.500 million bags up from 3.833 million bags produced the previous year. He said that this year the pre-harvest rains were much better than the year before. Vietnam is Asia's second-largest coffee producer, with robusta accounting for 95 percent of total production. It earned an estimated $425 million from exporting about 3.8 million bags of coffee in 1995/96, making the commodity Vietnam's fourth largest hard-currency earner. According to the Coffee Research Institute the area planted to coffee is around 200,000 ha about 30 times more than at the end of the Vietnam war in 1975. It was added that the average yield per ha was around 1.6 tonnes, much higher than a typical yield of 0.6 tonnes in other coffee-producing countries.

AUSTRALIA - Australia imported 76,500 bags of coffee in July 1996, 8.3 percent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 533,500 bags, 7.3 percent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 7.4 percent to 814,700 bags. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/July 1996 were Indonesia (66,800 vs 56,100 bags), Vietnam (135,900 vs 111,000 bags) and Papua New Guinea (153,100 vs 120,000 bags).
